question: Why do we divide attention scores by sqrt(d_k)?

criteria.description: variance of dot products grows with dimension d_k
large scores saturate the softmax so gradients vanish

rubric.modelAnswer: Dot products have variance that grows with d_k; large scores saturate the softmax and gradients vanish, so dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps variance near one.

answer: Because the variance of the dot products grows with the dimension d_k, large scores saturate the softmax and the gradients vanish.
